answers.assumption_check: Assumed: the ticket's commons state file is the only commons file a crossing moves (the artifact journal also moves; the measured commits show .artifact-journal.jsonl dirty in the class-space repo's own commits, so the journal's repo is unsettled and is read at build). 2026-11-19, read by cc_0 and confirmed by git show on origin: crossings 1648858dd (633a76c125d2) and 89447c4a6 (c408f2c1e66d), both DROPPED, committed only .artifact-journal.jsonl and cairn/devices/codemother/machines/clearance/{history,state}.json; the two tickets' commons state files stayed dirty until a hand commit, commons 0595ae5b3 ('633a76c125d2, c408f2c1e66d: DROPPED'). The ticket machine's published helper commit_crossing_records (ticket 79875eb17ac2, on its stacked branch, not yet landed) path-limits to the component's two files in the class-space repo only; the ticket's charter public_interface lists only Ticket and GATE_HOLDER.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs and has: Ticket.passed/failed in ticket.py, commit_crossing_records as the pattern (path-limited git -C), the commons work tree path from address.ROOTS, and the three clauses.
answers.children: none, because the work is one commit step in ticket.py and its proof
answers.collision_check: No real collision. 79875eb17ac2 and siblings commit the class-space half; this is the commons half, a separate repo and a separate commit.
answers.falsifier_check: Falsifier: after Ticket.passed or Ticket.failed on a ticket whose commons state file is tracked, git status --porcelain in the commons shows that state file clean, and a commit in the commons names it / another ticket's dirty file in the same commons work tree is not staged or committed by the crossing / a crossing whose ticket sits in no git work tree (a scratch commons) returns without raising. Horizon: the first reseal after landing.
answers.gates_bound: proved (Law 8: a proof a hollow build could not pass) and feeds back to origin on failure (Law 3): PROVEME runs the proof under the tester's seal on Linux; a red returns the ticket to FIXME.
